title: Web authentication with PKCE
goal: Users can sign in to the web app with Authorization Code + PKCE, stay signed in through short-lived in-memory access tokens and a rotating HttpOnly refresh cookie, and sign out cleanly, with no token ever in a URL or web storage.
scope_in: PKCE flow in apps/web/src/auth/: generate 64-char `code_verifier` with crypto.getRandomValues, S256 `code_challenge`, random `state`; redirect to `GET /v1/auth/authorize` with client_id `centcom-web`.

Callback route `/auth/callback`: validate `state`, exchange `code` at `POST /v1/auth/token` with grant_type `authorization_code`, header `X-Centcom-Client: web`, credentials included; strip query from history immediately.

Silent refresh using grant_type `refresh_token` with the cookie; single-flight across tabs via Web Locks (`navigator.locks.request('centcom-refresh')`) and BroadcastChannel to share the new access token.

Auth store (Zustand): `{status: 'unknown'|'anonymous'|'authenticated'; user?: Me; accessToken?: string (memory only)}` plus `useAuth()` and a fetch wrapper adding `Authorization: Bearer`, refresh-once-on-401 `token_expired` semantics from CT-ERR/CT-AUTH.
Route guards (`requireAuth`, `requireRole`) and sign-out: `POST /v1/auth/revoke` then clear store, broadcast to other tabs.
`GET /v1/me` bootstrap, exposing plan, active workspace and entitlement revision (`ent` claim) to other web lanes.
scope_out: Login methods (magic link, GitHub, Google): backend authorize page only.
Device flow (CLI, C052) and keychain storage.
Device key generation and registration for E2E (see notes, C083).
build_against: Mock backend (lane C007) implementing /v1/auth/authorize, /v1/auth/token, /v1/auth/revoke, /v1/me including 401 `token_expired`, `token_revoked`, `device_revoked` and `refresh_reuse_detected` scenarios; no real identity provider.
interfaces: export function startLogin(opts?: {returnTo?: string}): Promise<never>  // redirects
export async function completeLogin(url: URL): Promise<{returnTo: string}>  // callback handler
export function getAccessToken(): Promise<string>  // refreshes if exp within 60 s
export function useAuth(): {status; user?: Me; signOut(): Promise<void>}
export const authedFetch: (input: RequestInfo, init?: RequestInit) => Promise<Response>
acceptance: The authorize URL contains response_type=code, client_id=centcom-web, code_challenge_method=S256, a 43-128 char verifier-derived challenge, and `state` of >= 128 bits; `plain` challenge is never produced.
A callback with a mismatched or missing `state` aborts without calling /v1/auth/token and shows a neutral error with a 'Try again' action.
After callback, `window.location` contains no `code`/`state` query (history.replaceState) and localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB contain no access or refresh token (test scans all three).
Every request to /v1/auth/token carries `X-Centcom-Client: web` and `credentials: 'include'`; none carries a refresh token in body or URL.
Two tabs hitting expiry simultaneously cause exactly one refresh request (mock counts) and both end authenticated.

401 `token_expired` triggers exactly one refresh + retry; a second 401 signs out; `token_revoked`, `device_revoked`, `token_invalid` sign out without refresh; `refresh_reuse_detected` signs out and shows 'Signed out for your safety'.
Access token is refreshed when < 60 s remain (15 min lifetime); the timer survives tab sleep by checking on `visibilitychange`.
Sign-out calls /v1/auth/revoke, clears memory, and other open tabs become anonymous within 1 s.
tests: pkce.test.ts: RFC 7636 test vectors for S256, verifier charset/length.
refresh.singleflight.test.ts: two simulated tabs with Web Locks polyfill.
authedFetch.401.test.ts: table of all CT-AUTH 401 codes.
storage.scan.test.ts: asserts no token in any web storage.
guardrails: MUST NOT store access or refresh tokens in localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, cookies readable by JS, URLs or logs; access token lives in a module-scoped variable only.
MUST keep `code_verifier` only in sessionStorage between redirect and callback and delete it on first use (success or failure).
MUST use S256 only; MUST validate `state` in constant time; MUST reject callback if no pending login exists.
MUST serialise refreshes across tabs (Web Locks); concurrent refresh with a rotated token triggers `refresh_reuse_detected`, which revokes the whole token family.
MUST NOT follow open redirects: `returnTo` is a same-origin path validated against /^\/[A-Za-z0-9/_\-?=&.]*$/ and defaults to `/`.
Error screens MUST NOT echo server `detail` that contains anything but the CT-ERR `title`/`detail` text; no request ids in URLs.
failure_modes: Cookie blocked by browser (third-party/Safari ITP) -> after callback, refresh returns 401: show 'Your browser blocked sign-in cookies' with help link and keep user on /login.
Network down during refresh -> stay authenticated with expired token marked, retry with backoff 500 ms x2^n cap 30 s; requests queue max 20 for 10 s then fail with typed error.
Authorize returns error params (`access_denied`) -> neutral message, no details from the query rendered as HTML.
notes: CONTRACT GAP: PKCE authorize does not carry `device_pubkeys`, so no `dev_` identity or key registration exists for browsers; E2E in the web app (C083/C084/C085) cannot sign frames until the contract defines web device registration. CONTRACT GAP: CT-AUTH says web refresh cookie is scoped to /v1/auth/token; the `authorization_code` response body shape (access token field names) is taken from RFC 6749.
